chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man whose wealth was hidden from him for five years, then it came to him, so he did not reject the capital wealth. How much should he purify (pay Zakat on)? He (peace be upon him) said: 'One year'.
ai.seo_question: How is Zakat calculated on wealth that was hidden or inaccessible for multiple years?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'one year's Zakat' for wealth that was hidden or inaccessible for an extended period, reflecting the Shia juristic view that Zakat is not cumulative for years of absence unless the wealth was actively held and productive. It highlights the practical ease (taysir) granted to the owner upon recovery, distinguishing it from continuous wealth where Zakat accumulates annually. This ruling underscores the focus on the moment of possession and readiness for Zakat payment rather than mere duration of absence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rifa’at Bin Musa who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man whose wealth was hidden from him for five years, then it came to him, so he did not reject the capital wealth. How much should he purify (pay Zakāt on)?’ Heasws said: ‘One year’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rifa’ah ibn Musa who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man whose wealth remains lost for five years. He then finds it and does not reject the capital. How much Zakat is he required to pay? He (the Imam) said, ‘He pays one year’s Zakat only.’”
